title: Agentic Postgres workflow definition
description: One workflow a project publishes: an ordered list of steps, each naming a CAPABILITY of that project's compiled lock by name and version. This schema is the shape; the compiler is the meaning (ADR 0228). A file that validates here may still be refused at `bin/workflow.sh validate`, because what a step may name depends on the lock this project compiles and no schema can carry that.

schema_version.description: 1, the only version. A definition is installed as a row and is immutable per (name, version), so a second schema version is a decision about migrating rows and not only about parsing files.

name.description: The definition's name, unique with `version` across the project. The pattern is `app_private.workflow_definition.name`'s CHECK constraint, restated here so a name the table would refuse is refused in the checkout rather than at the deploy's step 6d.

version.description: The definition's version. A (name, version) already installed with a DIFFERENT source refuses the deploy (PT409): a definition is fixed forward by publishing a new version, the way a migration is (D912's rule for a definition).

description.description: What this workflow is for, in the author's own words. Required: a definition is a reviewed project artefact, and one nobody can read without compiling it is one nobody reviewed.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the whole run may take, measured from the first claim. Exceeded, the run fails as `timed_out` at the next claim -- it does not stop a call already in flight upstream.

steps.description: The steps, in the order they run. One at a time, each after the one before it succeeded.

name.description: The step's name, unique within the definition. NARROWER than the table's CHECK, which also admits a hyphen: a step's name is what a `{{steps.<name>.<field>}}` reference spells, and a reference grammar that admitted a hyphen could not be told from an expression.

capability.description: The capability this step calls, as `name@version`. A CAPABILITY and not a tool: a tool may be backed by several capabilities that move independently (`query_resource` is `query_notes` and `query_tasks`), so the tool name is not the versioned thing. The compiler resolves it to the tool that serves it, and to the resource for a relation read.

arguments.description: The arguments this step passes. Which names are accepted is decided by the lock, not here: a write's are the tool's declared argument list, a relation read's are `columns`, `filters`, `order_by` and `limit`, and an RPC read takes none. A string value may carry `{{input.<key>}}` or `{{steps.<name>.<field>}}` references, resolved per attempt by the worker.

retry.description: What to do with a RETRYABLE failure -- a transport error, a timeout, or the plane's own `write_conflict`. Every other outcome is terminal and is not retried, whatever this says.

max.description: How many retries, beyond the first attempt.

backoff_seconds.description: How long the step is PARKED before it becomes claimable again. The park is the backoff: nothing sleeps, and a worker killed during one loses nothing.

timeout_seconds.description: How long this step's call may take. Defaulted by the compiler from the tool's own `timeout_ms` when it is omitted, and refused when it is below that floor: a step timeout under the tool's would fail a call the plane was still willing to serve.

argument.description: A scalar, or a list of scalars. Not an object and not a nested list: an argument document the reviewed surface cannot receive is one the compiler would have to guess at, and `filters` -- the one argument with structure -- is a list of small objects the compiler checks by shape.
